newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Tequila sales up 20.97 percent in Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Tequila sales up 20.97 percent in Q1 1997.

text.p: Mexico's buoyant tequila industry chalked up a year-on-year increase of 20.97 percent in production volume during the first quarter of 1997, an industry body said on Friday.
A statement by the Tequila Regulatory Council said a total of 26,977,449 liters of the fiery brew were sold during the first three months of the year, compared with a year-ago figure of 22,299,697.
The Council added that of this total, 25.6 percent was made entirely from sugars derived from the agave cactus plant, with the remainder made from a blend of different sugars.

"Our 100-percent class presentation posted the strongest growth. Blended tequila grew 11.04 percent in the first quarter of 1997 when compared with the same quarter in 1996, while 100-percent tequila grew 62.44 percent," the statement said.
Growth in tequila produced for domestic consumption in the first quarter outstripped exports by 31.65 percent to 13.54 percent.
"Although our exports continue to grow, recovery in the domestic market has allowed domestic consumption to speed up," the statement added.
Of all tequila made in Mexico, 44.66 percent was for the home market in the first quarter, up from 41.04 percent in the same period last year.
